#7856. The Fall Essentials You Need According to 4 of the Most Stylish Guys We Know

The Fall Essentials You Need According to 4 of the Most Stylish Guys We Know

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1040 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor.
  • Fall has the singular ability to turn even the most Spartan man into a bit of a style savant.
  • It’s because fall invites more—more layers, more textures.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor. We may earn a commission from these links. Here’s how we test products and why you should trust us.

Fall has the singular ability to turn even the most Spartan man into a bit of a style savant. It’s like a wolf awakens the second that temperatures start to drop. Suddenly you see an Instagram post from the junior analyst below you; he must fancy himself a budding A$AP Rocky, because he’s rocking a statement scarf. Your brother-in-law is wearing a turtleneck. Your buddy is in white jeans. Every day, you zone out in dumb stakeholder meetings and fantasize about a newly introduced jacket or that pair of buttery-soft leather loafers you saw on a dude at the grocery store.

It’s because fall invites more—more layers, more textures. It can be freeing. No more worrying if that T-shirt will become a body scan of where and how you sweat; no more worrying if those pants will suffocate you. But ... it can be too much. How should you layer? How can you get funky for the holiday party without looking like an asshole? What brands are even worth buying?

According to recent reports, we answer all those questions elsewhere in this magazine, but today we want you to take a breath. Keep it simple. How? By following some good examples.

Industry observers note that A lot of the best-dressed guys right now are trimming down their wardrobes in favor of focusing on the basics. “This fall I’ve tried to trim the fat and make do with a much smaller wardrobe,” states actor, content creator, and friend of the magazine Albert Muzquiz—better known online by his handle @edgyalbert. “I only have a few shirts, a few pants, and a couple jackets—and I feel like I’m dressing better than ever.”.

So instead of lobbing a bunch of meaningless trends, or -cores, at you, we decided to send you to some of the best-dressed men of the moment. You’ve heard enough from us; here’s what they’re feeling this fall.

According to recent reports, jake Mueser, founder of the eponymous bespoke suiting brand J. Mueser, has a handful of fall essentials. That cohort includes a cream turtleneck, which “you can throw on with anything,” as well as a classic tweed or herringbone blazer—same idea. They’re easy but plenty damn sexy.

Mueser also extols the virtues of a classic flannel suit—perhaps like the one he makes. “It works with everything from a denim shirt to a tie,” he says. “I like to break it up, wearing the jacket with vintage light-wash Wrangler cowboy cuts.” (A move we wholeheartedly endorse.).

According to recent reports, J. Mueser Waverly Herringbone Virgin Wool-Tweed Blazer.

J. Mueser Ivory Chunky Merino Roll-Neck Sweater.

J. Mueser Charcoal Churchill Stripe Flannel Waverly Suit.

In a recent development, there are a few reasons Drew Thomas can’t stop recommending merino sweaters—the thin, almost jersey sort—to his more than 500,000 TikTok followers. “You can get so much wear out of one,” he states. “You can layer it in the fall, wear it on its own on a slightly warmer day, or tie it around your shoulders. It works in the spring too, and even on a summer night when it gets a little cooler.”.

Sources indicate that another seasonally versatile piece Thomas will stand ten toes down for is cream pants. In fact, Thomas likes to wear his all through fall. He keeps a few pairs on constant rotation. “I feel like the cream breaks up those darker fall colors and lets them stand out more,” he says.

According to recent reports, when it comes to his next fall investment, Thomas is taking cues from the British sartorial invasion (“It never really went away, but it definitely feels like it’s having a moment again”) and looking to Barbour. “Something timeless and practical that I can wear for years and that only gets better with age,” he says. “I love the idea of owning something that develops character over time and could eventually be passed down to someone else. Those are the kinds of pieces I feel are worth investing in.”.

Buck Mason Hollywood Pleated Trouser.

J. Crew Relaxed-Fit Double-Pleated Corduroy Pant.

Sources indicate that “A down vest is my favorite fall garment,” Esquire contributor Christopher Fenimore told us. “It’s an easy outerwear piece to layer stuff under. I run hot, and I like having parts of my body exposed to the elements.”.

It has been revealed that we second that, but more predictably he highlights the entire category of shirting. Jackets and layers get a lot of shine, but this is the layer that, no matter how much temperatures fluctuate, will be on the skin. It’s a great time to get a few good oxford-cloth button-downs, polos, or beefier tees.

Sources indicate that this time of year is also a great time to get clinical. “I assess things I have that might need updates, in terms of fit and silhouette or different fabrications depending on how I’d wear them,” he states. That can be rebuying your preferred undershirt or socks, or it could be a good time to jump on that thinner, more versatile merino sweater wave.

Rocky Mountain Featherbed Down Vest.

Industry observers note that “Fall is the best time to break in a new pair of denim,” Muzquiz claims. Wear it hard enough now and “it’ll be soft enough and possibly breathable enough for wear during the spring and parts of the summer.” No better time to get something esoteric.

Industry observers note that when it comes to fall shoes, Muzquiz is into a classic six-inch lace-up boot. “There are so many bullshit brands out there that are trying to fool you with budget options,” he indicates. “Just get a pair of Red Wing Heritage if you’re starting out or Viberg if you really wanna flex.”.

In a recent development, muzquiz also finds himself taking part in the “buttery, delicate loafer movement” that’s been picking up steam as of late. The Yardee Moccasin loafers from Vinny’s are his pick of the bunch.

Viberg Navvy Boot - Brandy Hatch Grain Calf.

Every Other Thursday Cashmere V-neck Knit.

Vinny’s Yardee Nappa Leather Loafer.

#7854. Survey: Most Organizations Are Not Consistently Measuring AI Value Against Costs

AI & Tech 📈 Bullish 🌐 Thejournal ↗ Open Full Page

Survey: Most Organizations Are Not Consistently Measuring AI Value Against Costs

📅 19 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (591 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A new study from consulting firm KPMG found that while AI investment continues to grow, relatively few organizations consistently measure whether the technology's benefits justify its costs.
  • Average planned AI investment for the next 12 months has risen to $210 million, compared with $186 million in the first quarter of 2026.
  • The findings are based on responses from 2,131 senior leaders across 20 countries and jurisdictions, surveyed between July 23 and August 26, 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new study from consulting firm KPMG found that while AI investment continues to grow, relatively few organizations consistently measure whether the technology's benefits justify its costs. The manufacturer's Global AI Pulse Q3 2026 report found that 89% of organizations report measurable value from AI, while just 12% consistently assess that value against costs across the organization.

Average planned AI investment for the next 12 months has risen to $210 million, compared with $186 million in the first quarter of 2026.

The findings are based on responses from 2,131 senior leaders across 20 countries and jurisdictions, surveyed between July 23 and August 26, 2026.

Most organizations have established ways to track AI spending: 61% review costs during project approval, and 59% monitor them once systems are operating.

In a recent development, consistently connecting those costs to value remains less common. Beyond the 12% that do so across the organization, another 26% assess value against costs for most initiatives.

In a recent development, organizations reporting established AI returns have stronger measurement practices. Among this group, 48% consistently assess value against costs, four times the proportion in the overall survey group.

Cost-monitoring dashboards are also more common among organizations reporting established returns: 77% use them, compared with 43% of those still experimenting.

Sources indicate that "The organizations seeing a return did the implementation and the transformation properly: guardrails in place, workforce ready, data cleaned up," remarked Priya Emmanuel, global head of aIQ at KPMG International. "That is a sequence, not a secret.".

Organizations are also developing more formal systems to manage AI deployment.

Fifty-five percent operate a formal AI management layer, which KPMG calls a "harness layer," comprising controls and tools between AI models and business applications.

In a recent development, security and identity controls, along with data access controls, were the most common capabilities, each reported by 43% of respondents. Model routing, which determines which model handles a particular task, was reported by 23%.

Meanwhile, 53% assign accountability for AI-informed decisions to a named executive, the CEO, or an executive committee.

The proportion reporting significant employee adoption of AI agents rose from 25% in the first quarter to 34% in the third quarter.

Cybersecurity concerns were more common among organizations with mature AI programs.

Half of those reporting established AI returns identified cybersecurity as a barrier, compared with roughly one-third of those still experimenting.

Overall, 86% of respondents stated their organizations are adapting their cybersecurity operating models to address AI-accelerated threats.

The report identifies accountability, operational resilience, and cost management as priorities as AI becomes more embedded in business operations.

Sources indicate that "Many organizations have made AI models widely available and track their use," remarked Swaminathan Chandrasekaran, head of the US AI Center of Excellence at KPMG. "But consumption alone is not a strategy.".

For the full report, visit the KPMG site.

Fall Is Almost Over, So I Rounded Up the 7 Celebrity Outfits I Still Want to Copy

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (681 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Like much of the TikTok generation, I spend way too much time looking for style inspo on social media.
  • Hollywood’s cool girls are squeezing every last wear out of fall, wearing silk midi skirts, sheer tops, and cape-like scarves.
  • While I can’t recreate every ensemble on the internet, I can round up the seven autumn outfits most on my mind, ranked by how eager I am to make them my own before the temps drop for good.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like much of the TikTok generation, I spend way too much time looking for style inspo on social media. While that sometimes means letting the dishes pile up in favor of a few extra minutes of scroll time, I rarely miss a street-style moment. Whether it’s Hailey Bieber in a date-night outfit or Taylor Swift in this season’s hottest color combination, I’ve been stowing away fall outfit inspiration for the final stretch of the season.

Hollywood’s cool girls are squeezing every last wear out of fall, wearing silk midi skirts, sheer tops, and cape-like scarves. Beyond fall essentials like trench coats and dark-wash denim, they’re also reaching for this year’s breakout trends, including maraschino-cherry-colored accessories and striped pullover sweaters, keeping their seasonal rotation fresh before winter takes over.

While I can’t recreate every ensemble on the internet, I can round up the seven autumn outfits most on my mind, ranked by how eager I am to make them my own before the temps drop for good. Keep reading for late-fall outfit inspo to carry you into the holiday season.

According to recent reports, on the set of Die Alive, Zoë Kravitz made a case for laid-back elegance and an unexpectedly bright fall color choice. The slinky midi skirt is polished, while the basic gray tank is casual. The trench coat makes the outfit perfect for chilly weather, with a pair of chocolate pumps elevating the style. Consider this your go-to look for weekend brunch prepares and cocktails with the girls alike.

Selena Gomez put a fresh spin on the capsule wardrobe, creating a monochromatic outfit using closet staples, including sleek capris, mesh pointed-toe heels, and a quilted cinched bag. However, instead of a basic black tee, she reached for a sheer iteration, turning the simple ensemble into a fresh and fun look. To pull it off for a chilly night, I’d add a leather bomber jacket.

Kristen Bell managed to wear just about every style trend at once—without it looking like a slop wardrobe. Her striped pullover served as the base, with coordinated fall-coded colors sprinkled throughout the rest of her outfit. Her dark-wash, wide-leg jeans reminded me why denim is an autumn classic, and I officially want her glove flats. However, it was Bell’s cherry-red beanie and merlot Chanel handbag that injected personality into her look.

Sources indicate that I’m all about a cozy fall wardrobe, but when date night rolls around, I want something a bit more elevated and sleek. Ashley Graham understood the assignment, wearing a silky plunge halterneck top and draped, gray trousers. While she opted for open-toe sandals, pointed, closed-toe pumps can beat the chill.

Karlie Kloss’ chic look is a nod to office wear. Her polished autumnal look features closet basics, including a white button-up shirt, above-the-knee skirt, and ballet flats. Kloss added an extra dose of flair by intentionally draping a black shawl across her shoulders, making it the perfect look for strolling Fifth Avenue and museum hopping alike.

Sometimes the best looks are the simplest. Daisy Edgar-Jones layered a classic white T-shirt underneath a sapphire-blue trench coat, taking a closet basic and elevating it with an unexpected twist. Light-washed, straight-leg jeans elongated her frame, and timeless black pumps turned a casual look into a polished ensemble.

Industry observers note that elizabeth Debicki played with fall textures, reaching for a bold leopard-print turtleneck sweater and slick leather pants. Leopard print is both timeless and trendy, which makes it especially easy to style. It’s the ideal outfit for a night on the town, perfectly cozy yet fashion-forward.

According to recent reports, ruby Ford-Dunker (McAuliffe) is a fashion and lifestyle journalist featured in Vogue, InStyle, Elle, Who What Wear, Marie Claire, Brides, the Upcoming York Post, Business Insider, and more. When she’s not reporting on her latest fashion obsession, she can be found listening to Taylor Swift, hunting for the best vanilla latte, playing with her cats, or smiling her way through a dance workout. Latest Update: Report: Cyber Attacks Increasingly Exploit Trusted Workplace Tools

📅 21 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (710 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In its latest threat intelligence report, Ontinue found that attackers are increasingly using trusted workplace tools to trick users into giving them access to enterprise networks.
  • Ontinue's report notes the trouble is that these attacks blend in with ordinary workday communication, which makes them harder to catch.
  • Sources indicate that "The majority of effective attacks today don't rely on sophisticated exploits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In its latest threat intelligence report, Ontinue found that attackers are increasingly using trusted workplace tools to trick users into giving them access to enterprise networks. Approximately 30% of organizations monitored by the cybersecurity tech giant experienced at least one attempt to impersonate IT support through Microsoft Teams during the first half of 2026. About one in every 990 external Teams contacts revealed signs of someone pretending to be an internal IT worker.

Ontinue's report notes the trouble is that these attacks blend in with ordinary workday communication, which makes them harder to catch.

Sources indicate that "The majority of effective attacks today don't rely on sophisticated exploits. They rely on trust," Balazs Greksza, director of Advanced Threat Operations at Ontinue, remarked in the company's announcement.

Recent findings suggest that ontinue broke down how a typical attack works: An employee gets an unexpected Teams message or call from someone claiming to work in the organization's IT department. The person warns of a security issue, a software problem or an enhancement that can't wait. Then they walk the employee through opening Windows Quick Assist, installing remote-access software, or running a PowerShell command. Following those steps can hand the attacker control of the employee's computer, often without the employee realizing it.

Sources indicate that the approach is very similar to the Black Basta ransomware group, which helped popularize similar attacks in 2024. Unfortunately, Ontinue found the technique has since been adopted by other cybercriminal groups, including some with no known link to Black Basta.

Sources indicate that some threat agents are also combining tactics. They might first overwhelm an employee's inbox with unwanted e-mails, then reach out through Teams pretending to be IT support offering to fix the problem.

"Phishing no longer resides solely in your inbox. It has spread across the entire corporate communications environment," said Mika Aalto, co-founder and CEO of Hoxhunt.

Teams impersonation is only part of the problem. Ontinue also found attackers taking advantage of legitimate Microsoft sign-in processes. Between May and June, researchers identified 10 confirmed device-code phishing compromises across five customer tenants.

Sources indicate that in these attacks, criminals trick employees into completing what appears to be a normal Microsoft authentication process. But doing so can give the attacker access to the employee's account and system without actually breaking their password.

The report also found attackers using blockchain-based infrastructure to hide malicious activity, accounting for more than 25% of confirmed malicious ClickFix findings.

"Attackers are no longer looking for gaps in your perimeter. They are looking for the systems your organization already trusts and finding ways to move through them undetected," stated Shane Barney, chief information security officer at Keeper Security.

It has been revealed that the security firm says that IT needs to keep a closer eye on unexpected Teams contacts, remote-support requests, suspicious PowerShell activity, and changes to authentication settings. Employees should also confirm sensitive requests through established internal channels, rather than relying on the name or account that appears on their screen.

Aviv Nahum, co-founder and CEO of Above Security, noted that AI is making these attacks more convincing by helping criminals imitate familiar voices, writing styles, and conversations.

"The security model therefore must shift from 'does this look real?' to 'can I independently verify that this person is who they claim to be?'" Nahum mentioned.

The full Ontinue report can be found here.

Chris Paoli (@ChrisPaoli5) is the associate editor for Converge360.

In an active social engineering campaign, cyber attackers are impersonating IT help desks and using fake passkey setup requests to compromise employee identities and gain access to enterprise cloud data.

A newly introduced study from consulting firm KPMG found that while AI investment continues to grow, relatively few organizations consistently measure whether the technology's benefits justify its costs.

Cybercriminals are moving away from mass phishing scams and focusing on more targeted attacks, often using trusted websites and services to trick victims, according to a latest report from KnowBe4.

Industry observers note that AI is moving beyond assisting cybercriminals and beginning to operate within live attacks, according to a recent report from Check Point Research. The technology is making sophisticated capabilities faster and more accessible while creating new security risks for businesses deploying their own AI systems.

Window treatments are often an afterthought, but your choice of drapery can make or break your entire design. Our 2026 Whole Home in Charleston is a master class in innovative design, and our designers took every opportunity to showcase their skills and style, down to the very last detail—including some gorgeous examples of transformative drapery.

It has been revealed that though often seen as a luxury, window treatments are a home necessity. Blinds, drapes, and shades don’t just line our windowpanes; they block drafts, light, and real-world clamor from entering your homes, practically on demand. While some choose to keep it simple, designers know your sill is uncharted territory for design potential. While it might be tempting to reach for your typical verticals, it’s worth making a statement. That stated, good drapes can be expensive, so if you’re hoping to embrace your window treatment’s potential, you’ll have to budget for it.

Industry observers note that in our patternmaxxed guest bedroom, designer Laura Lubin, founder of the Nashville-based design firm Ellerslie Interiors, used Stroheim drapes to add subtle color to her muted palette and elevate the chic TWOPAGES Roman shades just beyond. Then she took her design a step further: Instead of relying on pleating for texture, Lubin added a leafy trim and Fabricut bullion fringe to the edge of her panels, framing the bold blue baseboard and adding another note of texture to the room’s design.

Texture is meant to act as a bridge in design schemes, connecting elements and feeding both our visual and tactile appetites. In addition to her customized drapes, Lubin used grid-patterned wallpaper, natural wood grain, and plaid textiles to elevate the visual palette.

Industry observers note that if you’re looking for a quick bedroom upgrade with substantial impact, it might be time to take a closer look at your drapes. After all, your window treatments are meant to block out the world, not your style.

11 Winter Colognes You Can Get for Under $100

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1000 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that there’s never been a better time to get into personal fragrance.
  • So out with the fresh, aquatic, citrusy fragrances that belong on the beach and in with the warm, spicy, smoky scents that make the wintertime feel cozy.
  • If you’ve checked out any of our other affordable-cologne roundups, you won’t be surprised to see Cremo at the top of our list here.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there’s never been a better time to get into personal fragrance. The cologne market is booming with frequent fresh launches from luxury fashion houses and perfumeries, yes—but it’s also filled with tons of great scents from more accessible and affordable brands. And with the temperatures finally dropping below 50°F in New York and Thanksgiving coming up next week, we’re officially in winter mode. That means getting our puffer coats out of storage and changing up our seasonal fragrance rotation.

So out with the fresh, aquatic, citrusy fragrances that belong on the beach and in with the warm, spicy, smoky scents that make the wintertime feel cozy. We’re talking cardamom and cloves, smoky tobacco and incense, sweet vanilla and smooth amber. Want to capture the scent of sitting by the fireplace and sipping a hot cocoa while wearing a cashmere sweater? These scents will do that—and at a fraction of the cost of a designer fragrance. We rounded up our picks for the winter that all come in at under $100, so you can save the major bucks for holiday shopping.

If you’ve checked out any of our other affordable-cologne roundups, you won’t be surprised to see Cremo at the top of our list here. We talk about the brand a lot, but it’s for a good reason: Cremo’s colognes are some of our favorites out there, and they literally cost under $25 each. Spice & Black Vanilla is our favorite spicy scent from the lineup, and the warm blend of cardamom, vanilla, tobacco, and woods is perfect for winter. Wear it for a cold-weather date night, a fancy dinner, or really any occasion.

Want a decent cologne mist you can easily buy on Amazon for just $13? Old Spice has been around for almost 90 years—yes, it may remind you of your dad, but it’s been around for so long because it’s a classic that just works. But shaking things up a bit, the brand released a new collection of cologne mists earlier this year, which includes this Cashmere & Vanilla Wood scent bursting with spices and powdery iris. For $13, you might as well order a few.

Recent findings suggest that one of our favorite boozy colognes (and all-time favorite colognes in general) is Jazz Club from Maison Margiela’s Replica line. It’s one you’ve probably heard of and read about many times in our fragrance roundups, and since the 1 oz bottle is only $89, I just couldn’t leave it off this list. With rum, tobacco, and vanilla bean at the center, Jazz Club is the olfactory equivalent of sipping a cocktail in a smoke-filled bar. In other words, it’s the perfect sexy winter scent.

It has been revealed that gap recently introduced a new addition to its revitalized fragrance line (originally from the ’90s): Bliss. The gourmand EDP adds some creamy sweetness to the otherwise mostly fresh and earthy collection, and it came just in time for winter. It delights the senses with notes of butterscotch, cocoa bean, coconut milk, and vanilla bourbon, and it’s practically making my mouth water just thinking about it.

Industry observers note that huron has only five different scents, but it’s a true example of a brand that puts quality over quantity. I love each and every one of the brand’s EDPs, and while the marine Sea Salt + Driftwood and Original Citrus + Eucalyptus are both fresh and perfect for the summer, the Sandalwood + Black Pepper fragrance is definitely our winter choice. It’s warm, woody, and spicy, with some airy florals at the heart and rich amber and more woods at the base.

It has been revealed that if you like the scent of Tom Ford’s Oud Wood but can’t get past that $300 price tag, we hear you. That’s why House of Twist made Wood No. 28; it’s not exactly Oud Wood, but it’s close enough. And for just $48, we’ll take it. The fragrance is a nice blend of nutty cardamom, oud wood, vanilla, and creamy sandalwood—a combination pretty much anyone can get behind.

Making the cut at $99 is Phlur’s newest fragrance: Heavy Cream. It’s a rich gourmand that’s balanced out by some bright citrus and airy florals at the top and heart of the fragrance, so it doesn’t get too overwhelmingly heavy. It definitely has the notes you’d expect of a fragrance inspired by heavy cream, like vanilla, amber, and creamy musks.

Fine’ry is another one of our go-to brands when it comes to affordable colognes we actually like. And this winter, our top choice from the lineup is Smoke & Leather, which smells like—you guessed it—smoky tobacco and rich leather with some woody undertones. It definitely brings the heat on a cold day.

It has been revealed that boy Smells is known for pairing traditionally masculine and feminine scent notes for truly unisex fragrances that anyone can enjoy. Hinoki Fantôme is a fan favorite thanks to its blend of spices, woods, and smoke, which are underscored by earthy oakmoss, orris, and patchouli. You really can’t put this fragrance in one category, because it spans so many. It’s a complex fragrance that really works, especially for the winter.

Earthy scents are chameleons that can work in any season, so it really just matters what they’re paired with. In the instance of Stetson’s Free Rein from its new Untamed collection, the pairing of earthy notes of wild verbena, sweetgrass, prairie moss, and patchouli with vetiver smoke and red amber makes it a warm, rich fragrance that adds some heat to your cold-weather outfit.

Florals are, generally speaking, made for spring and summer—but sometimes you get a gorgeous blend of florals with woods, musks, or amber, and it becomes perfect for wintertime. That’s exactly what Lafco has done with its Golden Morning scent: It’s got light floral notes of apple blossom, lavender, violet leaf, and rose, which all play nicely with a rich, sweet base of woods, honey, amber, and musks.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, unauthorized artificial intelligence tools and agents are creating security risks for organizations as AI adoption increases, according to cybersecurity organization Sophos. In a recent product announcement, the company highlighted the growing use of shadow AI, referring to AI tools and agents operating without formal organizational approval or oversight. The security firm cited research indicating that 69% of organizations suspect or have evidence of unauthorized AI use.

Separate research from Gartner and Cloud Security Alliance found that 82% of organizations discovered shadow AI agents in their environments during the previous year.

According to the security firm, organizations have struggled to identify which AI tools employees use, what information those tools access, and whether their use complies with security policies.

"Organizations are adopting AI faster than they can secure it, and most security teams can't answer three basic questions: which AI tools are running, what data is going into them, and whether that activity lines up with policy," stated Kyle Falkenhagen, senior vice president of product management at Sophos.

The organization also cited an IDC projection that the number of AI agents could reach 1.3 billion by 2028.

Sophos researchers reported observing attackers use AI agents within a customer's network to build and test nearly 80 malware modules.

The cybersecurity firm revealed the general availability of Sophos AI Defense, a security offering designed to identify AI tools, monitor their activity, and enforce organizational security policies.

The product operates through Sophos Fusion, the firm's cybersecurity platform, and uses information from devices, networks, identity systems, and browsers.

According to the manufacturer, AI Defense can inspect prompts, uploads, and other AI interactions to identify potentially risky activity and help prevent sensitive data exposure.

For more information, go to the Sophos site.

A new study from consulting firm KPMG found that while AI investment continues to grow, relatively few organizations consistently measure whether the technology's benefits justify its costs.

Network-provider trust concerns are impacting enterprise AI looks, with AI and data-driven projects the most affected initiatives among respondents reporting disruption, according to a report from telecommunications provider Arelion.

SMART Technologies has introduced SoundFlow, a plug-and-play broadcasting system that allows classroom audio content to flow directly from a SMART Board display to students' compatible hearing aids, earbuds, headphones, personal listening devices, or speakers.

CrowdStrike's latest Threat Hunting Report traces a multiyear shift from conventional intrusions toward attacks that exploit trusted identities, cloud services, AI systems, and software dependencies.

Microsoft Expands AI Security Platform to Address Agentic AI Security Risks

📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (651 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Microsoft is expanding the scope of its AI-powered Project Perception security platform to address the growing concern that AI agents may have access to sensitive information and systems, yet don't always behave as expected.
  • In a organization blog post, Hayete Gallot, executive vice president of Microsoft Security, outlined how Microsoft prepares to use Project Perception to monitor, manage, and contain what it calls "agentic insiders." These are AI agents deployed within an environment that can access data, use software tools, and make decisions without constant human supervision.
  • "Agents are unpredictable," Gallot wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Microsoft is expanding the scope of its AI-powered Project Perception security platform to address the growing concern that AI agents may have access to sensitive information and systems, yet don't always behave as expected.

In a organization blog post, Hayete Gallot, executive vice president of Microsoft Security, outlined how Microsoft prepares to use Project Perception to monitor, manage, and contain what it calls "agentic insiders." These are AI agents deployed within an environment that can access data, use software tools, and make decisions without constant human supervision. While they can improve productivity, Microsoft warns that they also introduce security risks, even when they haven't been compromised by an attacker.

"Agents are unpredictable," Gallot wrote. "They will adapt as the context changes, may not behave as intended, and will collaborate and collude with other agents to reach their objectives, without needing to be compromised.".

Project Perception was first introduced in July. The platform, which entered public preview Aug. 3, is designed to help security teams respond to increasingly sophisticated cyber threats using AI-powered automation.

Instead of leaning only on traditional security alerts and manual investigations, Project Perception uses three kinds of specialized AI agents working together. Red team agents hunt for possible vulnerabilities, blue team agents look into suspicious activity, and green team agents step in to fix problems and strengthen defenses.

To spot threats and respond faster, the system pulls in security data from identities, endpoints, cloud environments, applications, and other sources.

Sources indicate that now Microsoft wants to use those same capabilities on the AI agents already running inside enterprise networks. Project Perception would find those agents, give them identities and permissions, and keep an eye on what they do across different systems. It would also keep assessing the risks that come with their actions.

In a recent development, microsoft also described a initiative for "Guardian Agents," specialized AI agents that supervise other agents and step in when their behavior gets risky. That might mean limiting an agent's permissions or blocking certain actions before they cause harm.

"Monitoring and securing those agents must become continuous," Gallot wrote.

In a recent development, the initiative also reflects concerns raised by Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella in an Oct. 10 essay on AI security.

Nadella argued that enterprises should treat powerful AI models much like potential insider security risks, particularly when those models can access confidential information or perform critical business operations.

"We simply can't outsource responsibility for what intelligence does on our behalf," Nadella wrote.

He called for security controls that operate independently of AI models, including restricted permissions, detailed activity logging, and mechanisms that allow administrators to stop an agent's actions.

"In other words, we need to separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it," Nadella wrote.

Microsoft admits that watching what AI agents do is only part of the answer. Gallot mentioned that future security tools will also need to show why AI models make the choices they do, not just what actions they end up taking.

For more information, go to the Microsoft blog.

Chris Paoli (@ChrisPaoli5) is the associate editor for Converge360.

In an active social engineering campaign, cyber attackers are impersonating IT help desks and using fake passkey setup requests to compromise employee identities and gain access to enterprise cloud data.

A new study from consulting firm KPMG found that while AI investment continues to grow, relatively few organizations consistently measure whether the technology's benefits justify its costs.

Cybercriminals are moving away from mass phishing scams and focusing on more targeted attacks, often using trusted websites and services to trick victims, according to a new report from KnowBe4.

AI is moving beyond assisting cybercriminals and beginning to operate within live attacks, according to a recent report from Check Point Research. The technology is making sophisticated capabilities faster and more accessible while creating new security risks for businesses deploying their own AI systems.

#7826. The Masculinity Defenders Are Already Whining About Robert Pattinson’s James Bond

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (887 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

The Masculinity Defenders Are Already Whining About Robert Pattinson’s James Bond

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (887 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After an exhaustive and exhausting years-long casting process, Robert Pattinson has been unveiled as the newly introduced James Bond, and right on cue, the masculinity defenders are being super normal about it.
  • In a recent development, I thought the significant takeaway was that we have the first James Bond with a cute little social media nickname (which led me to wonder whether we’d have been calling Pierce Brosnan “P-Broz” if there had been a Twitter in 1995).
  • Recent findings suggest that on a YouTube show called Dan Wootton: Outspoken, special guest and self-described “right-wing comedian” Leo Kearse noted Pattinson is “Not a man!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After an exhaustive and exhausting years-long casting process, Robert Pattinson has been unveiled as the newly introduced James Bond, and right on cue, the masculinity defenders are being super normal about it.

In a recent development, I thought the significant takeaway was that we have the first James Bond with a cute little social media nickname (which led me to wonder whether we’d have been calling Pierce Brosnan “P-Broz” if there had been a Twitter in 1995). But nope: the deal is that R-Patz is not manly enough to be the face of a film franchise that contains a movie called Octopussy.

Recent findings suggest that on a YouTube show called Dan Wootton: Outspoken, special guest and self-described “right-wing comedian” Leo Kearse noted Pattinson is “Not a man! He doesn’t have a hairy chest, no drink problem, he’s never bought a fridge.” Okay! Point by point: 1) Daniel Craig was smooth as a baby seal. 2) Watch The Lighthouse if you think R-Patz can’t convincingly put them away. 3) What?

Kearse, ignorant and undeterred as a real man ought to be, continues: “He probably still sleeps in a car shaped like a Ferrari, with Powerpuff Girls sheets.” Also he and Wootton both seem to be calling him “Robert Patterson” throughout. Great stuff. I mean this, Leo Kearse: you are the funniest right-wing comedian I’ve ever seen.

On X, Jesse Kelly made this point.

Interesting, except that the next Bond movie will be written by British screenwriter Steven Knight, who wrote the ultra-violent Eastern Promises, created the epic gangster series Peaky Blinders, and co-created Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?, which doesn’t have anything to do with James Bond or the broader masculinity conversation per se, but goddamn what a career.

In The Atlantic, Tom Nichols complained that “Pattinson lacks the manly gravitas …Pattinson is sensitive; he broods; he’s conflicted.” He concludes, “I imagine that when the mad criminal offers him a mint julep, Pattinson will scowl and explain that alcohol and sugar are bad for you.” Listen: if there’s anything more masculine than imagining a scenario and then getting angry at it, it’s fretting endlessly about what is and is not masculine.

Right under a piece whining that “the left-wing bias of The Grammys is on full display” (because Michelle Obama got a Best Audiobook nomination and Jesse Welles’s “No Kings” is nominated for Best Americana Roots Recording), the Blaze wrote a pretty straightforward news post about the casting, and although it’s journalistic malpractice to quote any comments section to prove any larger societal point, when you get comments like….

“Is he still licensed to kill, or will he be an unarmed social worker with a handbook on de-escalation negotiation?”.

On social media and comments sections and whatever that Dan Wootton show is, exhibit A for the case against Robert Pattinson’s masculinity is a 2023 Paris Fashion Week red carpet look: Pattinson in a fur jacket and a skirt. I don’t know, I think a man ought to defy conventions, go his own way, take some risks. Plus, the dude can rock a skirt. Don’t hate him because he’s beautiful.

Recent findings suggest that so Pattinson is too fey to play Bond, and too famous from other iconic roles besides. This is, of course, the exact criticism leveled at Roger Moore in 1972 when he took the role over: that he was too lithe to compete with the hairy-shouldered thickness of Sean Connery, and that he was already too well-known for having played a similar role in The Saint. (And for having done it on television; “TV Star” was an epithet until right around The Sopranos.) Timothy Dalton was dinged for being too Shakespearean to take over for Moore. Pierce Brosnan had already played a parody of a Bond type on Remington Steele, so how could he compete with the gravitas of Dalton? Daniel Craig was criticized for being too beefy to take over for Brosnan. You can’t win.

It has been revealed that the good news is that as much whining as there is about Pattinson and his lack of masculinity, there’s a lot less of it than there would have been even a few months ago. The “not man enough” chorus is singing, but they’re undeniably a little bit muted. Whether it has anything to do with Pete Hegseth and Markwayne Mullin and Sean Duffy and the rest of our government’s drag king grotesques of manliness publicly tripping on their dicks and compromising our basic security in the process I can’t say definitively, but it sure feels like it.

Among the many YouTube reaction videos, I came upon one that I am absolutely not going to watch, but whose title distills the argument down to its essence almost too perfectly.

In a recent development, there it is. I wanted someone else. The newly introduced thing is bad. The whole argument, like so many of the arguments against the evolution of masculinity, boils down to “things aren’t the way they were when I was younger, and I’m angry about it.” It’s the credo of the dull, the philosophy of the frightened, the logline of at least three Tim Allen sitcoms. Move on. Grow up. Let R-Patz cook.

I’ll meet you back here when we’re furious about Taylor Swift doing the theme song.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to a survey by data and AI services provider Further, enterprises are reporting benefits from artificial intelligence even as their data preparation and oversight processes remain incomplete.
  • It has been revealed that the company's recent State of Enterprise AI Maturity research surveyed 515 U.S.-based AI decision-makers.
  • In a recent development, the findings suggest that gaining value from individual AI applications and preparing to operate them more broadly are separate challenges.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to a survey by data and AI services provider Further, enterprises are reporting benefits from artificial intelligence even as their data preparation and oversight processes remain incomplete.

It has been revealed that the company's recent State of Enterprise AI Maturity research surveyed 515 U.S.-based AI decision-makers. Just 5% believed their organizations' data was largely ready for AI.

In a recent development, the findings suggest that gaining value from individual AI applications and preparing to operate them more broadly are separate challenges. Reported returns alone do not establish that an organization has the foundations to sustain or expand those results.

It has been revealed that further found that 37% of respondents' organizations had paused, scaled back, or abandoned an underperforming AI initiative in the previous 12 months. Among that group, data quality or availability was the most frequently cited main reason, at 24%.

Meanwhile, 29% reported completing a formal data audit and remediation blueprint. The research also placed 69% of organizations in the exploring, experimenting, or implementing stages of adoption.

According to recent reports, further distinguishes data prepared for conventional reporting from data prepared for AI. Its explanation emphasizes data origins and documentation, along with access controls that support ongoing evaluation and governance.

Sources indicate that for readers assessing their own readiness, the practical problem is whether data supports the requirements of a particular application. A collection suitable for a dashboard may need additional preparation before it can reliably support an AI system.

Industry observers note that seventy-seven percent reported a positive return on AI investment. However, only 3% stated their organizations had a documented AI-audit process.

It has been revealed that the findings measure different things: perceived financial benefit and the existence of a repeatable oversight process. Neither substitutes for the other.

"In reality, confidence without a documented process is exposure," stated Kierra Dotson, associate director of AI strategy and governance at Further. "Closing that gap doesn't take upcoming technology; it requires an auditable governance process.".

For the full report, visit the Further site (registration required).

A newly introduced study from consulting firm KPMG found that while AI investment continues to grow, relatively few organizations consistently measure whether the technology's benefits justify its costs.

Network-provider trust concerns are impacting enterprise AI intends, with AI and data-driven projects the most affected initiatives among respondents reporting disruption, according to a report from telecommunications provider Arelion.

SMART Technologies has introduced SoundFlow, a plug-and-play broadcasting system that allows classroom audio content to flow directly from a SMART Board display to students' compatible hearing aids, earbuds, headphones, personal listening devices, or speakers.

CrowdStrike's latest Threat Hunting Report traces a multiyear shift from conventional intrusions toward attacks that exploit trusted identities, cloud services, AI systems, and software dependencies.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the seventh annual Kips Bay Decorator Show House in Dallas returns to 2999 Turtle Creek Boulevard, but don’t expect it to look anything like it did in 2025.
  • Visit the show house and see each of the 22 designers’ rooms, from the first dedicated home gym in Kips Bay history by Dallas-based Platinum Gym Design, to a small but mighty European-inspired kitchen by Stephenson Home, to a 1970s-inspired primary bathroom fit with a glass brick shower and curtained-off water closet by Nuance Interiors.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the seventh annual Kips Bay Decorator Show House in Dallas returns to 2999 Turtle Creek Boulevard, but don’t expect it to look anything like it did in 2025. A upcoming group of the country’s leading designers has taken on the 25,000-square-foot French Renaissance estate, transforming each room to showcase bold ideas, highlight exceptional craftsmanship, and reveal the upcoming trends we can expect to see in the world of interior design.

Visit the show house and see each of the 22 designers’ rooms, from the first dedicated home gym in Kips Bay history by Dallas-based Platinum Gym Design, to a small but mighty European-inspired kitchen by Stephenson Home, to a 1970s-inspired primary bathroom fit with a glass brick shower and curtained-off water closet by Nuance Interiors. With sponsors like Benjamin Moore, The Shade Store, The Rug Tech giant, and more, the vibrant and personality-filled spaces come as no surprise.

As always, proceeds from the show house go to the Kips Bay Boys & Girls Club, which provides educational, enrichment, and developmental programs to thousands of young people, as well as Dallas-based nonprofits Dwell with Dignity and The Crystal Charity Ball.

According to recent reports, to see this celebration of exceptional design, you can purchase tickets here and visit the house from Saturday, November 14th to Sunday, December 6th. However, if you can’t make it to the Lone Star State in time, check out some of our favorite moments from the event below.

Sources indicate that kelsi Lamberth of Nuance Interiors pulled inspiration from the 1970s for her primary bathroom, separating the shower from the main prep space using a curved glass brick wall. The sculptural aspects can be found throughout in this groovy space.

In the primary bedroom, Troy Rivington of Rivington Marx Interiors cocooned the room in a dark floral wallpaper and accessorized with other moody botanicals throughout. He was inspired by the romance of 1940s Cairo, dressing the room up like it belonged to a well-traveled collector.

As the first ever dedicated home gym at the Kips Bay Show House, Peter Hoffman of Platinum Gym Design chose a refined, luxurious setup. He named the room Tanren after the Japanese art of hammering and refining metal, and used walnut in both the equipment and the ceiling slats, stainless steel frames, and brown leather accents to complete the exercise space.

In this bespoke bathroom, Russ Peters and Bill Cates of Peters Cates Design lined the wall behind the Studio McGee x Kohler bathtub with a rich merlot tile by RIAD Tile. It’s a beautiful statement and a fabulous way to bring more texture and dimension to the room.

Industry observers note that in this tucked away library space, filled with collected finds, designers Christina Garcia Lysaught and Grayson Knight of Layered Dimensions finished off this dark space with a stunning statement mirror. Around the perimeter are resin busts of wildlife, like owls and deer, bringing in a bejeweled touch to the room.

Sources indicate that the small but mighty kitchen, designed by Katie Stephenson of Stephenson Home, is crowned with a crackled-gold blooming wallpaper, bringing a warm balance to the rest of the room. It’s covered in birds, butterflies, and blossoms, and it wraps the cook space in a golden glow, reminding all who enter that this room should be as beautiful as it is functional.

Sources indicate that the citron paint color wrapping the walls in Jen Bienvenu’s entrance hall is undoubtedly enchanting and serves as the perfect backdrop for her “After the Hunt” theme, but it’s the lampshades made from old silk saris that tie everything together for us. They provide such a magical warmth and really capture the essence of a collector’s treasure room.

Related Story: Almost Every Piece in This Layered Arkansas Home Was a Lucky Antique Find.

Industry observers note that step through the citron entry and enter the round room, designed in collaboration by Helen Bergin Interiors and Lichten Architects. The walls are softened by long curtains from The Shade Store, which create beautiful juxtaposition with the curved, sculptural silver media console by Asher Gillman. The actual turntable is flush to the surface, giving it a seamless look while it emits wonderful sound.

In a recent development, in the Withdrawing Room by Jen Stevens of Fonde Interiors, plaster botanicals by artist Amanda Norman come to life as they crawl from the mantel along the chimney breast, escaping to the ceiling. The vines were handmade by Norman and capture the essence of a garden left undisturbed, showing that this formal-at-first-glance room has a wilder side.

The rosy palette in designer Jen Dean’s—founder of Jede Interiors—grand bathroom is topped off with a hand-painted floral mural that covers the ceiling. The rose-gold shine reflects the natural light in the room and give it more depth, while the natural motifs spread across the rest of the space.

Inside this observatory bedroom by sisters Amy Mobley and Katie Norrid of City Hill Design, the Verellen bed is raised up from the ground on a custom platform, emphasizing the importance of the furniture’s role in this space meant for relaxation and rest. It’s wrapped in a striped silk carpet that beckons your touch with a chartreuse mohair sofa at the foot.

Related Story: A Trip to the Lone Star State Inspired the Earthy Textures of This Tennessee Upcoming Build.

Colorful and collected, this vibrant library by designer Betsy Wentz is not visually quiet. The maximalist space is covered in pattern-mixed Schumacher from ceiling to floor, and the designer pumped up the volume by opting for this triangular table in this tucked away corner.

In designer Amy Switzer’s textural bar lounge—filled with plush chairs, unique artwork, large tassel accessories, and beaded cigarettes—it’s the stone details that really make the room sing. Onyx cornices crown the windows, blue agate inlays decorate the floor, and a banquette which curves around a custom stone and wood table bring a natural coolness to the room that only stone can bring.

#7817. It’s Time to Talk About “Duty Sex”

It’s Time to Talk About “Duty Sex”

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (984 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that there are certain things that belong on your chore list: Doing laundry, washing dishes, taking the trash out, scrubbing the toilet.
  • Duty sex typically stems from good intentions, Marisa Derr, LMFT explains.
  • This isn’t just an unnecessary pressure that can be demoralizing, it’s also just super unsexy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that there are certain things that belong on your chore list: Doing laundry, washing dishes, taking the trash out, scrubbing the toilet. Sex, as you can see, is not one of those things—and it shouldn’t be. And yet, “duty sex” has become a pretty recognizable term in today’s relationships.

Duty sex typically stems from good intentions, Marisa Derr, LMFT explains. This happens when one partner wants to keep the peace or protect the relationship. It’s when you have sex because for some reason or another, you feel like you have to—not because you’re worried for your safety, but you believe that the success of your relationship lies on “fulfilling” some sexual duty.

This isn’t just an unnecessary pressure that can be demoralizing, it’s also just super unsexy.

“The problem is that sex out of obligation teaches the body that intimacy is another task, and desire fades even more,” she says. “Over time, the partner initiating feels rejected, and the partner saying yes feels used, even though neither one wants that.”.

Recent findings suggest that there’s an important distinction between duty sex and what we call “willing consent.” Willing consent is when you’re not necessarily feeling desire for your partner in the moment, but you consent to a sexual interaction with them because you’re open to desire showing up. It’s like when you’re not feeling particularly hungry, but you know that you really enjoy a certain meal so you go out to eat at the spot anyway. Duty sex is born from obligation, rather than curiosity—like eating that weird casserole your aunt brings on Thanksgiving when you really don’t want to, but do anyway because you prefer to not ruffle any feathers.

When did sex with our partners become that weird casserole or equivalent to scrubbing the toilet?

According to a recent study in Evolutionary Psychology, duty sex can be rooted in fear: Fear that a partner will cheat, fear that one could be less attractive than their partners and need to somehow “make up for it,” and fear that a partner will lose interest in them.

Industry observers note that and while we typically assign duty sex as something that women mostly do—particularly because of the pressures to perform that disproportionately affect women—the study revealed that men were having duty sex at similar rates as women. Though, more research is needed to find out if there is a difference between why men have duty sex and why women do it.

The thing that most people having duty sex had in common was that they were in long-term relationships.

“Couples can start worrying about how often they're having sex, rather than whether they're actually enjoying it,” sex educator Anna Richards tells Cosmopolitan. “But intimacy shouldn't be about meeting a target or keeping score. It should be something you both genuinely want.”.

Sources indicate that sex should be about feeling pleasure and connecting with your partner in a fun, sexy, and intimate way. But for some couples, somewhere in the midst of all of the responsibilities of everyday life, sexual desire was put on the back burner. And instead of working to get it back, people are essentially forcing themselves to have duty sex to maintain their relationships. We need a serious overhaul of partnered sex!

Sources indicate that “You can't demand desire, but you can create an environment where it has room to grow,” Richard states. Think about what the study noted about why people have duty sex: they’re afraid of losing their partner. And one of the ways to bridge this gap of insecurity is to foster a relationship that comes with reassurance. If you’re the one finding yourself having duty sex, communicate with your partner about the pressure you feel. Talking about your needs—whether they come in the form of emotional security, verbal affirmations, or quality time—can help your partner learn how to help you foster desire. And if you’re the partner that’s noticing your S.O. initiate sex just to check it off a list, maybe it’s time to think about whether you’re reassuring them enough in the relationship. Do you create an environment of trust and comfort? Are you caring? Do you help them with their daily tasks?

According to recent reports, one of the best ways to remove sex off your to-do list and onto your want-to-do list is to take it off your list completely. That may sound counterintuitive, but Richards says it helps alleviate the pressure.

Industry observers note that “Intimacy doesn't always have to lead to the bedroom,” she indicates. Flirting, spending quality time together, being affectionate, making each other feel appreciated, talking about what you enjoy—these can all help rebuild a connection between you and your partner.

“Sometimes removing the expectation is exactly what allows desire to return naturally,” she says. You also need to make sure that your relationship is a place where saying “no” feels safe.

“A yes only means something when a no is fully okay,” Derr explains. “Pressure, sulking, or keeping score kills desire.”.

It’s also about the little things. Saying “thank you” when they do something nice, touching each other throughout the day, complimenting each other, and just being a good partner can all lend themselves into reigniting desire.

In a recent development, life is way too short to be having sex because you feel like you have to. Plus, any healthy and happy relationship would not foster an environment where sex feels like a duty in the first place. Yes, making a relationship work longterm does take work and effort—but that doesn’t mean that every aspect of your relationship should feel like work. The parts that are meant to be fueled by fun and curiosity (like sex) should remain fun. And the second sex starts feeling like a chore, it may be time to clear your checklist and make reconnecting your first priority.

Latest Update: How to Watch Every Movie in the Marvel Cinematic Universe

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2338 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Suddenly, we’re excited about Marvel again.
  • Anyway, it’s been seven years since we last saw a fresh Avengers movie.
  • Here’s how to watch every Marvel movie before Avengers: Doomsday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Suddenly, we’re excited about Marvel again. Hitting theaters on December 18 is Avengers: Doomsday, the long-awaited next Avengers sequel. You may have heard that Robert Downey Jr. is back, only now in the role of the villainous Doctor Doom instead of Iron Man. As the man himself said back at San Diego Comic-Con in July 2024: “New mask, same task.” Whatever that means. (Also, if you think you ever heard of something called Avengers: The Kang Dynasty, no, you didn’t.).

Anyway, it’s been seven years since we last saw a fresh Avengers movie. Back then, you might have Googled something like, “How to watch every Marvel movie.” I have a gut feeling that’s what brought you here now. As Doomsday awakens dormant feelings about superheroes and multiverses, you probably need a guide to help you revisit all the best Marvel films or catch up on the ones you’ve missed. Lucky for you, it is easy to catch up. You just need time and a Disney+ subscription. If you start now, you’ll roll credits on The Fantastic Four: First Steps by December 17.

Here’s how to watch every Marvel movie before Avengers: Doomsday. Check back a year from now, when we’re doing it all over again for Avengers: Secret Wars.

It has been revealed that here’s the good news: Except for Spider-Man: Brand Upcoming Day, which came out this summer and is now on digital, every Marvel Cinematic Universe movie is available on Disney+. Every. Single. One.

It has been revealed that iron Man? Yes. Infinity War? Yup. Captain America: The Winter Soldier? Hell yeah. Guardians of the Galaxy? All three, baby! Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania? Maybe skip that one. And since Disney acquired Fox in 2018, you’ll also find all the X-Men, Deadpool, and the two Fantastic Four movies from the mid-2000s.

There’s also plenty of Marvel television. Not just streaming shows like WandaVision, The Falcon and the Winter Soldier, Ms. Marvel, and the recent VisionQuest, but also network shows like Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. and Agent Carter, as well as the Netflix Defenders-verse. If you’re really hardcore, you can also watch the handful of “One Shot” short films that were originally released on several Blu-rays.

Recent findings suggest that the only “Marvel movies” you can’t watch on Disney+ are (most) of the Sony-produced movies. These include Morbius, Madame Web, Kraven the Hunter, and the Venom trilogy. But because distribution rights are funny, the Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield Spider-Man movies are on Disney+, along with Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse as I write this.

I hear you. Short of time-traveling back to 2000 and watching every movie as they come out, it feels impossible to “catch up” with all of it now. Especially since Avengers: Doomsday is once again dealing with the multiverse, which means even “non-canon” movies (like, say, the Blade or Punisher movies) might get a shout-out.

Recent findings suggest that luckily, Marvel knows your pain. On Disney+, a fresh “Countdown to Avengers: Doomsday” sub-page highlights the most crucial movies. While there are glaring omissions, watching only the highlighted movies can bump just about anyone up to speed. Even people who say they’ve “never seen one of these things.”.

Sources indicate that for your convenience, I’ve listed below EVERY movie from the Fox X-Men universe, the Sony Spider-Man universes, and the Marvel Cinematic Universe, in order of theatrical release. This is the only correct “viewing order.” Do not listen to YouTubers who insist on some “timeline order” nonsense. You can be an adult and watch these things exactly how they were produced and released. The movies Marvel deems essential for Doomsday prep are listed in bold, with the trailers attached.

You’re welcome. Now get assembled.

Blade is rightfully credited with kickstarting the 21st-century superhero boom, but the X-Men films set the tone as must-see summer blockbusters. The first film in Fox’s X-Men series introduced audiences to mutants, with Hugh Jackman as Wolverine, the late Patrick Stewart as Charles Xavier, and Ian McKellen as radical extremist Magneto, who leads his Brotherhood in a fight for equal rights. Famke Janssen and James Marsden, who also starred as Jean Grey and Cyclops, respectively, will return in Doomsday, but Halle Berry’s Storm is sitting it out.

Recent findings suggest that the battle for mutant liberation continues when Colonel Stryker (Brian Cox) kidnaps Xavier, forcing the X-Men to align with the Brotherhood of Mutants. In this better-than-you-remember sequel, mutantkind stands side by side for the sake of their survival. Though X2 predates shared universes, its scope, scale, and political intrigue make it one of the greatest and most underrated sequels of all time.

“I am Iron Man.” The resurrection of Robert Downey Jr.’s career blasted off to the stratosphere, along with the Marvel Cinematic Universe itself, in a movie that officially kicked off the MCU. Kidnapped by terrorists and forced into a cave with scraps, playboy futurist Tony Stark (Downey Jr.) escapes as the armored superhero Iron Man and returns home to find that his enemies are far closer to him than he suspects. When the smoke clears, a shadowy figure named Nick Fury (Samuel L. Jackson) informs him that the universe is way bigger than he knows.

X-Men Origins: Wolverine (2009).

Once, Chris Evans was the Human Torch. Suddenly, he wasn’t. As the Marvel Cinematic Universe picked up steam, the sweltering summer of 2011 saw Captain America: The First Avenger. Set in World War II, the first Marvel “prequel” stars Evans as the brave shrimp of Brooklyn, Steve Rogers, who becomes the first to endure the experimental “Super Soldier” program. As Captain America, Rogers takes the fight to Red Skull, whose dark ambition lies beyond the Third Reich.

There once was an idea: To bring together a remarkable group of cinematic superheroes to see if they can make cinematic history. In 2012, Marvel did just that. The first crossover Avengers movie saw the growing roster of Marvel’s cinematic superheroes team up for the very first time. Though Marvel movies have only gotten bigger and even better since, we cannot deny the seismic impact of The Avengers.

Captain America: The Winter Soldier (2014).

The Amazing Spider-Man 2 (2014).

X-Men: Days of Future Past (2014).

Captain America: Civil War (2016).

Industry observers note that guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 (2017).

Industry observers note that after The Avengers planted the seeds for Thanos, all of Marvel’s storytelling shifted to an adaptation of the 1991 comic crossover The Infinity Gauntlet. In 2018, Marvel released Avengers: Infinity War, the third Avengers movie that forever changed the MCU’s status quo. With Josh Brolin as Thanos, the Marvel Universe’s many heroes band together to stave off the greatest threat anyone had ever seen. While audiences knew another movie was around the corner, its shock ending dared to ask the unthinkable: What happens when heroes lose?

According to recent reports, it all came down to this. In 2019, on the same weekend Game of Thrones staged its own final battle, Avengers: Endgame changed the trajectory of the Marvel Universe once more. The fourth Avengers film sees the heroes dust off for a rematch against Thanos. But before they can do that, they must travel back in time through their own history to collect the Infinity Stones if they want to stand a chance.

In September 2026, in preparation for Doomsday, Marvel released an extended cut of Avengers: Endgame, titled Encore. It comes with a few extra minutes of scenes that frankly ruin the grace of Endgame in its original form, but if you really want to see clearer connective tissue to Doomsday, check out Encore.

Spider-Man: Far From Home (2019).

According to recent reports, in the 1970s, one of the most popular Marvel Comics titles wasn’t The Amazing Spider-Man, Uncanny X-Men, or The Avengers. It was Master of Kung Fu, starring an ass-kicker named Shang-Chi. He was a master martial artist and the son of a supervillain (Fu Manchu in the comics) who, over time, works as a secret agent for MI6. He was created by Steve Englehart and Jim Starlin (who also created Thanos) in the spirit of Bruce Lee and the TV show Kung Fu.

After decades of obscurity, the box-office success of Crazy Rich Asians in 2018 inspired Marvel to dig into the longboxes and put the spotlight back on Shang-Chi. In 2021, Simu Liu brought him to life in Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, an origin movie that introduces Shang-Chi for the 21st century. Hong Kong screen legend Tony Leung (In the Mood for Love) costars as Wenwu, Shang-Chi’s father, who runs the terrorist group the Ten Rings—named after Wenwu’s mysterious alien weapons—which kidnapped Tony Stark in the first Iron Man.

In a recent development, shang-Chi’s use of the Ten Rings has yet-unknown ties to the wider Marvel Universe. After five years, we may finally have some answers in Avengers: Doomsday.

Venom: Let There Be Carnage (2021).

After Spider-Man was publicly unmasked as Peter Parker at the end of Spider-Man: Far From Home, the teenage superhero turns to Sorcerer Supreme Doctor Strange (Benedict Cumberbatch) for help. But when the magic goes wrong, the multiverse cracks open, and villains from other realities—as in, other Spider-Man franchises—seep through the cracks. Tom Holland’s Spider-Man teams up with two veteran Spideys, played by Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield (remember them?), to put the universe back in one piece.

Doctor Strange saved the universe in Avengers: Endgame and restored the multiverse in Spider-Man: No Way Home. But can he save himself? In this direct sequel to 2016’s Doctor Strange and set after both Spider-Man: No Way Home and the Disney+ series WandaVision, Stephen must help protect a young girl, America Chavez (Xochitl Gomez), from a vengeful Wanda (Elizabeth Olsen), who wants to use America’s unique powers to reunite with her own lost family.

Sources indicate that originally billed as Marvel’s first horror movie (its very title alluding to Lovecraft’s At the Mountains of Madness), creative reshuffling led to Evil Dead and Spider-Man director Sam Raimi helming the movie. This explains the movie’s uniquely darker tone than one might expect from a typical Marvel tentpole. Cameos in this film tie directly to some of Marvel’s other far corners, like TV demonstrates What If...? and Inhumans, as well as the Fox X-Men movies.

Werewolf by Night (2022), a “Marvel Studios Special Presentation” on Disney+.

The real-life passing of Chadwick Boseman in 2020 left a huge hole in everyone’s hearts—and Marvel in a difficult place. Without its star, writer/director Ryan Coogler redesigned his intends for the sequel to his Earth-shattering 2018 hit.

Recent findings suggest that taking inspiration from Reginald Hudlin’s run in the comics, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever sets the stage for a latest Black Panther: Shuri, T’Challa’s genius sister, played by Letitia Wright. But before Shuri can take up her brother’s mantle, she must first learn how heavy crowns are when another kingdom emerges from the depths and threatens Wakanda. The sequel introduces Namor (Tenoch Huerta), from the underwater world Talokan (originally Atlantis in the comics). The two will play a larger role in Avengers: Doomsday.

The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special (2022), a “Marvel Studios Special Presentation” on Disney+.

Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania (2023).

Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 (2023).

After Hugh Jackman retired from playing Wolverine in the 2017 masterpiece Logan, Marvel and Ryan Reynolds shelled out a truckload of money to get him back and into some yellow spandex at last. The third movie in the Deadpool series, Deadpool & Wolverine, marked the MCU debut of Ryan Reynolds’ scrotum-faced Deadpool, whose dream of joining the Avengers clashes with the collapse of his own reality. More cameos, callbacks, and cusses fill the movie’s two-hour runtime.

Sources indicate that while Jackman and Channing Tatum—who was once tapped to play the X-Men member Gambit, which Deadpool & Wolverine finally made a reality—will return in Doomsday, it’s unknown whether Reynolds will too. But if his surprise appearance at Comic-Con means anything, then...

When Steve Rogers gave Sam Wilson (Anthony Mackie) the shield of Captain America in Endgame, Sam wasn’t ready to take up the responsibility so soon. He still had his own things to work out. After the Disney+ series The Falcon and the Winter Soldier, Sam now flies the skies as Captain America, with the 2025 film Captain America: Brave New World marking the start of his era as the Star-Spangled Man. In addition to being the fourth Captain America movie, the movie revisits the events of 2008’s The Incredible Hulk and 2021’s Eternals.

The Marvel franchise was built on a studio elevating comic book benchwarmers into A-listers. That tradition was upheld in the 2025 movie Thunderbolts*. Based on a Marvel Comics series where supervillains form a team, the big-screen version recruits several “forgotten” antiheroes from different corners of the MCU. Together, they form a new team that must stave off their own assassination and save the world—on their terms. You can watch the movie cold, but know that many of these characters come from movies like Captain America: The Winter Soldier, Black Widow, Ant-Man and the Wasp, and the TV show The Falcon and the Winter Soldier.

And now, we step into a whole ‘nother world. After multiple attempts at a significant-screen Fantastic Four, the Marvel Cinematic Universe launched its own take on the First Family in The Fantastic Four: First Steps. Set on a different Earth in 1964, the Fantastic Four rise to the occasion when the planet is threatened by Galactus.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day (2026).

Recent findings suggest that look. Don’t put yourself through that. There are too many. If you insist on watching any of them, just watch Loki. It has two seasons and just 12 episodes total, so you can knock it out in one weekend. Loki takes place after Avengers: Endgame (technically after just The Avengers, but how and why is too long to explain), and of all the shows, it bears the strongest ties to Doomsday. Talk about a glorious purpose.

Industry News: Researchers Find AI Is Accelerating Vulnerability Discovery
